The world is at tick 12000 and 1,080 organisms are alive. No one else was in the world, so they should all be mine. I didn't call report or observe at the end, so I don't have the final count per lineage.

**What held the population back:** sugar. Every death was starvation, and the world settled at roughly 1,000 organisms from about tick 2000 onward, whatever I released.

**How each genome did:**
- **grazer1** (radius 3, two sugar sensors): my first genome, which carried the population all game at about 690–770 alive. It ate the most per organism, but its upkeep was also the highest at 0.0205 per tick.
- **grazer2** (radius 2, cheaper): it barely moved, so it ate little. It fell to 22 alive by tick 10000 and was extinct by 11750.
- **drifter3** (radius 2, mouth and a weak flagellum, no sensors): the cheapest design that held up, with upkeep of 0.009 per tick. It established itself at about 230–240 alive.
- **drifter4, drifter5 and a second batch of drifter3** (released at ticks 6000 and 8000): all went extinct. Once the sugar was used up, new founders starved before they could breed, even with lower upkeep.

**The last-minute boost:** founders in this world lived about 400 ticks before starving. So at tick 11750 I spent the whole remaining budget (625) on 125 founders of **sitter6**, a mouth-only body with upkeep of 0.006 per tick. They only needed to survive 250 ticks to count.
